problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Quadratic Form on the Unit Sphere
examples.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=x_1^2-2x_2^2-2x_3^2+2x_2x_3$  given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d7716e2c2924212e880275dd674d4a951daf66ac41e5a888a57acb6be686118f.png)

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +3) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(\lambda +3)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =1,\,-1,\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = -3.
$$

feedback.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5{x}_{1}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=3(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 3.$ 

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=3.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =5(0)+3(1)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $3.$
